title: Beyond Weight Updates: Evolving Agent Harnesses for Domain Specialization
why: Casts domain specialization as evolving the frozen-policy agent harness (system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding) with a GEPA-style reflective outer loop, and reports that harness adapters recover most of the gains of weight updates at lower compute and compose with RL.
mechanism: Outer-loop harness evolution over system prompt, tool schemas, skill library, and planning scaffolding while the policy stays frozen; instantiated with GEPA and evaluated as loadable per-domain adapters that can be combined with weight-based RL.
evaluation_signal: Authors report experiments with Codev, a Claude Code-style coding agent, on SWE-bench Verified, OfficeBench, and Terminal-Bench: weight updates give the strongest single-path gains, harness evolution recovers most of those gains at a small fraction of the compute, and combining both paths is best overall; they also analyze an SFT failure mode of shortened reasoning chains and increased truncation that harness adapters avoid by construction.
evidence_locator: Abs title, opening framing, method claim (GEPA outer loop / harness adapters), and experiment/result sentences on Codev and the three benchmarks.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.AI /new listing abstract and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 19 Nov 2026). No public code URL on the abs page. Full PDF not read.

title: Evolve Where It Matters: Coverage-Guided Self-Evolution of Agent Skills
why: Introduces SkillPlumber, in which an agent revises its own packaged skills using instruction-level coverage labels (follow / not-follow / not covered) so that self-evolution targets missing or unfollowed instructions rather than whole-run outcomes.
mechanism: Coverage-guided skill self-evolution: a persistent root-cause agent turns coverage labels into revision questions and checks each revision on the next run, while a maintainer distills investigations into a shared strategy library.
evaluation_signal: Authors report results across three benchmarks and three executors: SkillPlumber solves 64.7% to 70.5% of tasks, 25.6 to 30.4 points above the initial skill and 8.7 to 14.0 points above the strongest baseline; removing coverage reduces recovered failures by 20.8% on SkillsBench with GPT-5.5.
evidence_locator: Abs method paragraph (instruction-level coverage and SkillPlumber) and the reported benchmark/ablation sentences.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.CL new and cs.AI cross listing abstracts and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 19 Nov 2026; 15 pages, 5 figures). No public code URL on the abs page. Full PDF not read.

title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
why: A systematic (and largely negative) study of feedback-free skill rewriting: models rewrite expert skills round after round with no task, run, or judgment, then agents are evaluated with the rewritten skills; the paper also proposes SkillDiff, which marks expert knowledge the model would not write on its own.
mechanism: Feedback-free self-evolution of agent skill documents by repeated model rewriting without execution feedback, plus SkillDiff, which marks in place the expert knowledge that lies outside a model's prior without changing the skill text.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that every tested model performs worse with the rewritten skills on every benchmark, by 15 points on average on SkillsBench after thirty rounds; putting the lost out-of-prior knowledge back recovers much of the pass rate, and SkillDiff raises the SkillsBench pass rate by 4.8 points on average without feedback or text changes.
evidence_locator: Abs study design, the SkillsBench 30-round drop, the prior-sampling analysis, and the SkillDiff result sentence. Project repository linked from the abs page.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.AI /new listing abstract and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 19 Nov 2026). Official repo https://github.com/LitaoGuo/How-Self-Evolution-Reshapes-Skills is linked on the abs page (created 2026-10-23). Full PDF not read.

title: Meta-RTL: Evolving Agent Harnesses for RTL Optimization
why: Evolves the executable search procedure (the RTL optimization harness) from a minimal loop with EDA feedback, holding the optimization model, EDA flow, and per-design budgets fixed, and transfers the evolved harness to unseen designs without further evolution.
mechanism: EDA-grounded evolution of RTL optimization agent harnesses from a minimal loop; the search procedure is the retained object, while the model, EDA flow, and budgets stay fixed. Compared against hand-engineered Dr. RTL. Characterizes three search mechanisms in the evolved harness via ablations.
evaluation_signal: Authors report that Meta-RTL* reduces aggregate WNS/TNS violations by 7.8%/11.0% versus Dr. RTL across 20 development designs, with area reductions on 70% of them; without further evolution it transfers to 10 unseen IC-RTL designs, reducing aggregate WNS/TNS violations by 20.5%/14.0% and total synthesized area by 12.6%.
evidence_locator: Abs framing (hand-engineered vs evolved harnesses), the development-set comparison to Dr. RTL, the unseen-transfer sentence, and the ablation/case-study claim.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.AI /new listing abstract and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 19 Nov 2026; 7 pages, 5 figures). No public code URL on the abs page. Related to, but distinct from, already-collected Dr. RTL (2611.13713). Full PDF not read.

title: System-One RSI: Building Muscle Memory for Interactive Agents through Guided Practice
why: Couples a fast inner OODA loop (decision model plus decision tree, no reasoning model at action time) with an offline outer loop in which reasoning agents revise the decision-model prompt and decision tree from interaction records—retained as external muscle memory—while also optionally training or deploying updated model parameters.
mechanism: Two-loop System-One RSI: an online Observe-Orient-Decide-Act cycle uses a decision model and a decision tree for timed actions; an offline team of reasoning agents revises the prompt and decision tree, derives supervision from captured interaction records, and may train or deploy updated parameters. The improved system returns to the environment for the next round. Harness components (prompt, decision tree, external muscle memory) are retained; weight updates are also part of the described outer loop.
evaluation_signal: Authors report a 27B decision model in Snake, Zenless Zone Zero, and Black Myth: Wukong. Mean Snake score increases from 1.30 to 7.35; in an evaluated Zenless Zone Zero scenario, median completion time decreases by 8.4%; in an evaluated Wukong combat scenario, the evasive policy achieves 11 times the mean survival time of a stationary reference, and the offensive policy win rate rises from 0% to 66.7% across the evaluated configurations. The framework is described as operating with a small number of real episodes and without expert demonstrations or simulation.
evidence_locator: Abs two-loop description (inner OODA and outer revision of prompt, decision tree, and optional weights) and the Snake / Zenless Zone Zero / Wukong result sentences.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.AI /new listing abstract and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 19 Nov 2026; 19 pages, 9 figures, 5 tables). No public code URL on the abs page. Full PDF not read.

title: Sage-Evolve-Preview:Adaptive Observation for Post-Training Self-Improvement
why: Treats observation as the evolved harness component in post-training RSI: the anchor benchmark stays fixed, while a controller refines diagnostic granularity, escalates difficulty, and adds related tasks when aggregate anchor scores stop revealing actionable gaps.
mechanism: AdaObs, described as an observation-side mechanism of harness evolution. At a plateau, a controller refines diagnostics, escalates difficulty, and adds related tasks; validated increments are fused back into training, while every checkpoint remains evaluated against the fixed anchor objective.
evaluation_signal: Authors report eight independently optimized anchors in long-context reading comprehension and instruction following: AdaObs raises the mean score from 66.4 to 73.7 under a matched data budget, outperforming FixedObs (the anchor-only baseline). The evolved harness further improves the seven-task average on the independent PostTrainBench across two agent backends.
evidence_locator: Abs framing of exhausted observation vs exhausted capability, the AdaObs mechanism paragraph, and the eight-anchor / PostTrainBench result sentences.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.AI /new listing abstract and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 19 Nov 2026). Title on abs/API has no space after the colon. The described loop still includes training (weight updates); the claimed contribution is harness-side observation adaptation. No public code URL on the abs page. Full PDF not read.

title: Steering Automated Scientific Discovery via Audited Epistemic Exploration
why: A plug-and-play research-agent scaffold (EpiCompass) that retains an epistemic tree of hypotheses, evidence, beliefs, and revisions, then uses unresolved conflicts and unexplored directions to steer later hypothesis generation and to audit the final conclusion against accumulated evidence.
mechanism: EpiCompass maintains a retained epistemic tree during an investigation, reassesses explored hypotheses against accumulated evidence, selects candidates by anticipated epistemic gain (refinement vs expansion), and verifies the final conclusion against that evidence.
evaluation_signal: Authors report results across three scientific-discovery benchmarks and three LLM backbones, stating consistent outperformance of baselines and further analyses showing reductions in unsupported claims and failures to revise beliefs.
evidence_locator: Abs scaffold description (epistemic tree / anticipated epistemic gain / conclusion verification) and the three-benchmark, three-backbone result sentence. Comments field: Technical Report.
retrieval_notes: Opened Friday 20 Nov cs.AI new and cs.CL cross listing abstracts and the abs HTML (v1, submitted 18 Nov 2026, first announced on this Friday list). No public code URL on the abs page. Full PDF not read. Scope is a retained discovery scaffold rather than a cross-task self-improving loop.
